title: HPLC Laboratory Build / Recovery
organization: St. Joseph's Hospital and Medical Center — Phoenix, AZ
mandate: Develop and standardize a body-fluid amino-acid HPLC capability into a CAP-recognized biochemical genetics section.
objective: Establish a functioning clinical biochemical-genetics section with validated methods, SOPs, quality assurance, proficiency testing, LIS reporting, training, document control, budget/purchasing, and research extension.
resources_controlled: capital requests exceeding $1,000,000 (human-attested; amount not independently documented)
execution: Cultivated a body-fluid amino-acid HPLC analyzer into a standardized biochemical-genetics section recognized by CAP.
Authored SOPs for instrumentation, LIS, and specimen processing.
Established training procedures, guidelines, and skill-evaluation documentation.
Validated and maintained quality assurance; developed CAP proficiency policies and recurring inspection-readiness processes.
Implemented document control and integrated/launched LIS data reporting.
Managed budget and purchasing, instrumentation, reagents, and specimen analysis.
Established clinical trials and designed/presented research applications extending the laboratory.
Human additionally characterizes the inherited project as initially nonfunctional/dead-on-arrival.
validation: Historical resume documents recurring CAP inspection/proficiency requirements and quality-assurance maintenance.
Public 2009 MALDI-TOF publication independently confirms related St. Joseph's/Barrow mass-spectrometry research authorship, but not the HPLC section build itself.
outcomes: Historical resume documents conversion of the HPLC capability into a standardized biochemical-genetics section recognized by CAP.
